title.zh: 卷九十 列傳第十五 二劉殷許程柴任丘
title.en: Volume 90 Biographies 15: Two Lius, Yin, Xu, Cheng, Chai, Ren, Qiu
title.raw: 卷九十 列傳第十五 二劉殷許程柴任丘 Volume 90 Biographies 15: Two Lius, Yin, Xu, Cheng, Chai, Ren, Qiu

sentences.zh: 劉弘基

translations.literal: Liu Hongji
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hongji

sentences.zh: 劉弘基，雍州池陽人。

translations.literal: Liu Hongji was a native of Chiyang in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hongji came from Chiyang in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少以廕補隋右勛侍。

translations.literal: In youth he entered office through privilege as a Right Merit Attendant of the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he received a hereditary appointment as a Right Merit Attendant under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 大業末，從征遼，貲乏，行及汾陰，

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye reign he followed the expedition to Liaodong; short of supplies, he had advanced only as far as Fenyin,
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Daye era he marched on the Liaodong campaign; his funds ran out before he had reached Fenyin,

sentences.zh: 度後期且誅，遂與其屬椎牛犯法，諷吏捕系。

translations.literal: he reckoned that arriving late would mean execution, so with his followers he slaughtered an ox in violation of the law and baited officials into arresting them.
translations.idiomatic: realizing that missing the deadline meant death, he and his men slaughtered an ox to break the law and maneuvered officials into arresting them.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，以贖論，因亡命，盜馬自給。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was sentenced to ransom, then fled as an outlaw and stole horses to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he was released on payment of a fine; he then went into hiding and stole horses to live on.

sentences.zh: 至太原，陰事高祖。

translations.literal: Reaching Taiyuan, he secretly attached himself to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Taiyuan he quietly pledged himself to Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 又察太宗資度非常，益自托。

translations.literal: He also observed that Taizong's capacity and bearing were extraordinary and relied on him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: He also saw that the future Taizong possessed uncommon talent and placed himself under him all the more firmly.

sentences.zh: 由是蒙親禮，出入連騎，間至臥內。

translations.literal: Thereupon he enjoyed personal favor, riding in and out with him; at times he even entered the sleeping quarters.
translations.idiomatic: From this he won intimate favor, riding out and in with him, and sometimes even entering his private chambers.

sentences.zh: 兵將舉，弘基募士，得二千人。

translations.literal: When the army was about to rise, Hongji recruited men and obtained two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: As the uprising was about to begin, Hongji raised troops and gathered two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 王威等鯁大事，弘基與長孫順德伏閤後，麾左右執之。

translations.literal: When Wang Wei and others obstructed the great undertaking, Hongji with Changsun Shunde lay in ambush behind the gate and ordered attendants to seize them.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Wei and others blocked the great plan, Hongji and Changsun Shunde hid behind the gate and had their men seize them.

sentences.zh: 從攻下西河，宋老生敗，棄馬投塹，弘基斬其首，拜右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He followed the attack that took Xihe; when Song Laosheng was defeated and abandoned his horse in a ditch, Hongji beheaded him and was appointed Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the capture of Xihe; when Song Laosheng was routed and threw himself from his horse into a ditch, Hongji took his head and was made Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 師至蒲，引兵先濟河，下馮翊。

translations.literal: When the army reached Pu, he led troops first across the river and descended on Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Pu he led his men across the river first and took Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 為渭北道大使，命殷開山副之。

translations.literal: He was made envoy of the Weibei Circuit and Yin Kaishan was named his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed envoy of the Weibei Circuit, with Yin Kaishan as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 西徇扶風，眾至六萬，南度渭，次長安故城，振隊金光門。

translations.literal: He marched west through Fufeng, his force reaching sixty thousand; crossing the Wei southward, he encamped at the old city of Chang'an and displayed his ranks at Guangming Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He swept west through Fufeng until his host reached sixty thousand; crossing the Wei to the south, he encamped at the old site of Chang'an and paraded his troops at Guangming Gate.

sentences.zh: 隋將衛文升來拒，弘基逆擊，擒甲士千餘，馬數百。

translations.literal: Sui general Wei Wensheng came to resist; Hongji met him in counterattack and captured more than a thousand armored soldiers and several hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui general Wei Wensheng came to oppose him; Hongji struck back and took more than a thousand armored men and several hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 時諸軍尚未至，弘基最先勝。

translations.literal: At the time the other armies had not yet arrived; Hongji was first to win.
translations.idiomatic: The other armies had not yet come up, but Hongji won first.

sentences.zh: 高祖悅，賜馬二十匹。

translations.literal: Gaozu was pleased and bestowed twenty horses.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was delighted and gave him twenty horses.

sentences.zh: 京師平，功第一，授右驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified his merit ranked first and he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was secured his achievement stood first, and he was made General-in-Chief of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 討薛舉，戰淺水原，八總管軍皆沒，唯弘基一軍戰力，矢盡，為賊拘。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Xue Ju, they fought at Qianshui Plain; the eight commanders' armies were all lost, but only Hongji's army fought on until arrows were exhausted and he was seized by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Xue Ju they fought at Qianshui Plain; all eight commanders' forces were destroyed, but Hongji's alone kept fighting until his arrows were spent and the enemy took him.

sentences.zh: 帝以臨難不屈，優護其家。

translations.literal: The emperor, because he had not bent in peril, treated his family with special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had not yielded in danger, the emperor gave his household exceptional care.

sentences.zh: 仁杲平，乃克歸，官之如初。

translations.literal: When Ren Chuo was pacified he was able to return and his office was restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ren Chuo was subdued he made his way back and was reinstated in his former post.

sentences.zh: 劉武周犯太原，弘基屯平陽，復陷賊。

translations.literal: Liu Wuzhou invaded Taiyuan; Hongji garrisoned Pingyang and again fell into the rebels' hands.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wuzhou attacked Taiyuan, Hongji held Pingyang and was captured by the rebels again.

sentences.zh: 俄自拔歸，授左一總管。

translations.literal: Before long he broke free and returned, and was appointed Left First Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he escaped and returned, and was named Left First Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 從秦王屯柏壁，以勁卒二千繇隰州趨西河，躡賊歸路。

translations.literal: Following the Prince of Qin at Baibi, with two thousand crack troops he took the route via Lizhou toward Xihe and trailed the enemy's line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Prince of Qin at Baibi, leading two thousand elite troops by way of Lizhou toward Xihe to cut off the enemy's retreat.

sentences.zh: 賊銳甚，弘基堅壁儲勇。

translations.literal: The enemy was very fierce; Hongji held the walls and stored his strength.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were at their peak; Hongji shut himself in the fort and husbanded his forces.

sentences.zh: 及宋金剛遁走，率騎尾之介休，與王合擊，大破之。

translations.literal: When Song Jingang fled, he led cavalry in pursuit to Jiexiu and joined Wang in attack, routing them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Jingang fled, he led cavalry in pursuit to Jiexiu and, joining forces with the Prince, smashed them completely.

sentences.zh: 累封任國公。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Ren.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed repeatedly until he became Duke of Ren.

sentences.zh: 從擊劉黑闥，還，除井鉞將軍。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Liu Heita, on return he was made General of the Well Battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: After campaigning against Liu Heita he returned and was appointed General of the Well Battle-axe.

sentences.zh: 會突厥患邊，督步騎萬人備塞，自豳北東拒子午嶺，西抵臨涇，築障遮虜。

translations.literal: When the Turks harried the frontier he directed ten thousand foot and horse to guard the passes, from north of Bin east to Ziwu Ridge and west to Linjing, building barriers to block the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks troubled the border he commanded ten thousand infantry and cavalry to guard the frontier, from north of Bin eastward to Ziwu Ridge and westward to Linjing, erecting barriers to hold off the nomads.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，李孝常等謀反，坐與交，除名為民。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan, Li Xiaochang and others plotted rebellion; for association with them he was struck from the rolls as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan, when Li Xiaochang and others conspired rebellion, he was demoted to commoner status for associating with them.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，起為易州刺史，復封爵。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was recalled as prefect of Yi Prefecture and his noble rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was recalled as prefect of Yi and his title was restored.

sentences.zh: 召授衛尉卿，改封夔國。

translations.literal: Summoned and made Minister of the Court for the Imperial Clan, his fief was changed to the state of Kui.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and made Minister of the Court for the Imperial Clan, with his fief changed to the state of Kui.

sentences.zh: 以老乞骸，為輔國大將軍，朝朔望，祿賜同職事。

translations.literal: Citing age he asked to retire; he was made Mighty General Who Assists the State, attending court on the first and fifteenth of the month with stipend and gifts equal to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Citing old age he asked to retire and was made Mighty General Who Assists the State, attending court on the first and fifteenth of each month with salary and gifts equal to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 太宗征遼，召為前軍大總管，戰駐蹕山，有功，累加封戶至千一百。

translations.literal: When Taizong campaigned against Liaodong he was summoned as Grand Commander of the Forward Army; fighting at Mount Zhubei he had merit and his enfeoffment households were repeatedly increased to eleven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong campaigned against Liaodong he was recalled as Grand Commander of the Forward Army; at Mount Zhubei he distinguished himself, and his enfeoffment households were raised in stages to eleven hundred.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈開府儀同三司，并州都督，陪葬昭陵，謚曰襄。

translations.literal: On death he was posthumously made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the same protocol as the Three Excellencies, Governor of Bingzhou; he was buried beside Zhaoling with posthumous title Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Privileges Equal to the Three Excellencies and Governor of Bingzhou; he was buried beside Zhaoling with the posthumous title Xiang.

sentences.zh: 始，弘基病，給諸子奴婢各十五人，田五頃，謂所親曰：「使賢，固不藉多財；

translations.literal: When Hongji first fell ill he gave to each of his sons fifteen slaves and attendants and five qing of fields, telling those close to him: "If they are worthy, they surely do not need much wealth;
translations.idiomatic: When Hongji first fell ill he gave each of his sons fifteen slaves and five qing of land, and told those close to him: "If they are capable, they hardly need great riches;

sentences.zh: 即不賢，守此可以脫饑凍。」

translations.literal: if they are not worthy, holding to this they can escape hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: if they are not, holding to this they can still escape hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 余悉散之親黨。

translations.literal: The rest he distributed entirely among kin and friends.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else he gave away among relatives and friends.

sentences.zh: 子仁實，襲封。

translations.literal: His son Renshi inherited the fief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Renshi inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 殷開山

translations.literal: Yin Kaishan
translations.idiomatic: Yin Kaishan

sentences.zh: 殷開山，名嶠，以字行，世居江南。

translations.literal: Yin Kaishan, named Qiao, was known by his style; his family had long dwelt south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Kaishan, personal name Qiao, was known by his style; his family had long lived in the south.

sentences.zh: 祖不害，仕陳為司農卿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Buhai served Chen as Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Buhai had served Chen as Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 陳亡，徙京兆，為鄠人。

translations.literal: When Chen fell they moved to the capital region and became natives of Hu.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen fell they moved to the capital region and became residents of Hu.

sentences.zh: 開山涉書，工為尺牘，為隋大谷長。

translations.literal: Kaishan was versed in books and skilled at letters; he served Sui as magistrate of Dagu.
translations.idiomatic: Kaishan was learned and skilled at correspondence; under the Sui he was magistrate of Dagu.

sentences.zh: 高祖兵起，召補大將軍掾，從攻西河。

translations.literal: When Gaozu raised his army Kaishan was summoned as senior clerk to the great general and followed the attack on Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu raised his army Kaishan was recruited as staff officer to the great general and joined the attack on Xihe.

sentences.zh: 為渭北道元帥長史。

translations.literal: He was chief clerk to the commander of the Weibei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief clerk to the Weibei Circuit commander.

sentences.zh: 時關輔群盜驁力自張，不相君，命開山招慰，皆下。

translations.literal: At the time bandits in the passes each lorded their strength and would not bow to one another; he was ordered to summon and comfort them and all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits in the Guanzhong region each flaunted their power and refused to submit to any leader; Kaishan was sent to win them over, and all came down.

sentences.zh: 與劉弘基屯故城，破衛文升之兵，賜爵陳郡公，遷丞相府掾。

translations.literal: With Liu Hongji he garrisoned the old city, defeated Wei Wensheng's troops, was given the title Duke of Chen Commandery, and was promoted to staff officer in the Chancellor's Office.
translations.idiomatic: With Liu Hongji he held the old city, defeated Wei Wensheng's force, was enfeoffed as Duke of Chen Commandery, and was moved to the Chancellor's staff.

sentences.zh: 以吏部侍郎從秦王討薛舉。

translations.literal: As Vice Minister of Personnel he followed the Prince of Qin against Xue Ju.
translations.idiomatic: As Vice Minister of Personnel he accompanied the Prince of Qin against Xue Ju.

sentences.zh: 會王疾甚，臥營，委軍於劉文靜，誡曰：「賊方熾，邀速戰利。

translations.literal: The Prince fell gravely ill and lay in camp; he entrusted the army to Liu Wenjing and charged him: "The enemy is now flourishing; invite swift battle for profit.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince fell seriously ill and lay in camp; he entrusted the army to Liu Wenjing and warned him: "The enemy is at full strength—seek a quick victory.

sentences.zh: 公等毋與爭，糧盡眾枵，乃可圖。」

translations.literal: You others must not contend with them; when grain is exhausted and the masses are weakened, then you may plan.
translations.idiomatic: Do not engage them yet; when their grain is gone and their men are spent, then you may act.

sentences.zh: 開山銳立事，說文靜曰：「王屬疾，憂公弗克濟，故不欲戰。

translations.literal: Kaishan was eager to achieve something and told Wenjing: "The Prince being ill fears you cannot succeed, and therefore does not wish to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Kaishan was eager to make his mark and urged Wenjing: "The Prince is ill and fears you cannot finish the task, so he does not want to fight.

sentences.zh: 今宜逗機制敵，無專以賊遺王也。

translations.literal: Now you should seize the moment to control the enemy; do not insist on leaving the enemy for the Prince alone.
translations.idiomatic: You should seize the moment and control the enemy—do not leave the whole burden to the Prince when he recovers.

sentences.zh: 請勒兵以怖之。」

translations.literal: Please array the troops to intimidate them.
translations.idiomatic: Please array the troops and overawe them.

sentences.zh: 遂戰折墌，為舉所乘，遂大敗。

translations.literal: They then fought and were broken at Zheyi, taken advantage of by Ju, and utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: They gave battle at Zheyi, were caught by Ju's counterstroke, and suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 下吏當死，詔貸之，除名為民。

translations.literal: He was judged worthy of death but pardoned by edict and struck from the rolls as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: He was handed to the law as deserving death, but an edict spared him and he was struck from the rolls as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 頃之，從平仁杲，復爵位，兼陜東道行臺兵部尚書，遷吏部。

translations.literal: Before long, following the pacification of Ren Chuo, his noble rank was restored and he served concurrently as Minister of War of the Eastern Circuit of Shaanxi and was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, after the pacification of Ren Chuo, his title was restored; he served concurrently as Minister of War on the Eastern Shaanxi circuit and was later transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 從討王世充，以功進爵鄖國公。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Wang Shichong, for merit he was advanced to Duke of the State of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Wang Shichong he earned merit and was advanced to Duke of Yun.

sentences.zh: 征劉黑闥，道病卒，王哭之慟，詔贈陜東道大行臺右僕射，謚曰節。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Liu Heita, he died of illness on the road; the Prince wept bitterly for him and an edict posthumously made him Right Vice Director of the Eastern Circuit of Shaanxi with posthumous title Jie.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Liu Heita he died of illness on the march; the Prince mourned him deeply, and an edict posthumously made him Right Vice Director of the great Eastern Shaanxi office, with the posthumous title Jie.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十四年，與淮安王神通、河間王孝恭、民部尚書劉政會俱配饗高祖廟廷。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhenguan, together with the Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong, the Prince of Hejian Li Xiaogong, and Minister of the People Liu Zhenghui, he was granted paired sacrifice in Gaozu's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhenguan he was granted joint sacrifice in Gaozu's temple hall together with the Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong, the Prince of Hejian Li Xiaogong, and Minister of the People Liu Zhenghui.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，加贈司空。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era he was posthumously further raised to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yonghui era he was posthumously further honored as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 劉政會

translations.literal: Liu Zhenghui
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhenghui

sentences.zh: 劉政會，滑州胙人。

translations.literal: Liu Zhenghui was a native of Zuo in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhenghui came from Zuo in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，為太原鷹揚府司馬，以兵隸高祖麾下。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he was military adjutant of the Sui Hawk-and-Bolt garrison at Taiyuan and his troops were under Gaozu's command.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era he was adjutant of the Hawk-and-Bolt garrison at Taiyuan, and his troops served under Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 王威等既貳，秦王欲先事除之，遣政會為急變書告其反。

translations.literal: When Wang Wei and others wavered, the Prince of Qin wished to act first and eliminate them; he sent Zhenghui with an urgent report denouncing their rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Wei and others turned disloyal, the Prince of Qin wished to strike first and sent Zhenghui with an urgent memorial accusing them of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 時募士已集，乃執威等囚之，然後舉兵，政會功也。

translations.literal: By then the recruited men were assembled; they then seized Wei and the others and imprisoned them, after which they raised the army — Zhenghui's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: By then the recruits were assembled; they seized Wei and the others and only then raised the army—this was Zhenghui's doing.

sentences.zh: 大將軍府建，為戶曹參軍，遷丞相府掾。

translations.literal: When the Great General's Office was established he was Household Registrar and was promoted to staff officer in the Chancellor's Office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great General's Office was set up he was Household Registrar, then moved to the Chancellor's staff.

sentences.zh: 武德初，授衛尉少卿，留守太原，調輯戎政，遠近歡服。

translations.literal: At the start of Wude he was made Vice Minister of the Court for the Imperial Clan, remained to guard Taiyuan, adjusted frontier administration, and near and far rejoiced in submission.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Wude he was made Vice Minister of the Court for the Imperial Clan and left to guard Taiyuan; he put frontier affairs in order and won submission near and far.

sentences.zh: 會劉武周寇并州，晉陽豪傑舉應之，政會為武周所擒，每密表賊形勢。

translations.literal: When Liu Wuzhou raided Bingzhou the magnates of Jinyang rose to join him; Zhenghui was seized by Wuzhou and repeatedly sent secret memorials on the enemy's situation.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wuzhou attacked Bingzhou the leading men of Jinyang rose for him; Zhenghui was taken by Wuzhou but kept sending secret reports on the enemy's movements.

sentences.zh: 既平，復官爵，歷光祿卿，封邢國公。

translations.literal: Once pacified his office and title were restored; he served as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and was enfeoffed Duke of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: After the region was pacified his rank was restored; he served as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and was enfeoffed Duke of Xing.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，轉洪州都督，卒。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan he was transferred as Governor of Hong Prefecture and died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he was transferred to Governor of Hong Prefecture and died there.

sentences.zh: 太宗手詔：「政會昔預義舉，有殊功，葬宜異等。」

translations.literal: Taizong wrote in his own hand: "Zhenghui in the past joined the righteous rising and had exceptional merit; his burial should be of a special grade.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong wrote in his own hand: "Zhenghui took part in the righteous rising and rendered exceptional service; his funeral should be of a special grade.

sentences.zh: 於是贈民部尚書，謚曰襄。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was posthumously made Minister of the People with posthumous title Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore posthumously made Minister of the People with the posthumous title Xiang.

sentences.zh: 後追徙渝國。

translations.literal: Later his fief was changed to the state of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Later his fief was changed to the state of Yu.

sentences.zh: 子玄意襲爵，尚南平公主。

translations.literal: His son Xuanyi inherited the title and married the Princess of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuanyi inherited the title and married the Princess of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 高宗時為汝州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Gaozong era he was prefect of Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong he served as prefect of Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 次子奇，長壽中，為天官侍郎，薦張鷟、司馬锽為監察御史，二人因申屠瑒以謝，奇正色曰：「舉賢本無私，何見謝？」

translations.literal: His second son Qi, in the Changshou era, was Vice Minister of the Celestial Office; he recommended Zhang Zhuo and Sima Zheng as inspecting censors; the two thanked him through Shen Tu Yang; Qi said sternly: "Recommending the worthy is without private favor — why thanks?
translations.idiomatic: His second son Qi, in the Changshou era, was Vice Minister of the Celestial Office; he recommended Zhang Zhuo and Sima Zheng as inspecting censors; the two tried to thank him through Shentu Yang, but Qi said sternly: "Recommending talent is not a private favor—why thank me?

sentences.zh: 聞者皆竦。

translations.literal: Those who heard it were all awed.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard it were struck with awe.

sentences.zh: 後為酷吏陷，被誅。

translations.literal: Later he was trapped by a cruel official and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was framed by a cruel official and executed.

sentences.zh: 七世孫崇望

translations.literal: Seventh-generation descendant Chongwang
translations.idiomatic: Seventh-generation descendant Chongwang

sentences.zh: 七世孫崇望，字希徒，及進士第，宣歙王凝辟轉運巡官。

translations.literal: Seventh-generation descendant Chongwang, styled Xitu, passed the jinshi examination; King Ning of Xuan and She recruited him as patrol officer for transport.
translations.idiomatic: His seventh-generation descendant Chongwang, styled Xitu, passed the jinshi examination; Prince Ning of Xuan-She recruited him as transport patrol officer.

sentences.zh: 崔安潛帥許及劍南，崇望昆弟四人同幕府，世以為才。

translations.literal: Cui Anqian commanded Xu and then the Sword South circuit; Chongwang and four brothers served together in his staff, the age deeming them talented.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Anqian commanded Xu and then the Sword South circuit, Chongwang and four brothers all served in his staff, and the age regarded them as a talented clan.

sentences.zh: 安潛入為吏部尚書，崇望又以員外郎主南曹，選事清辦。

translations.literal: Anqian entered the capital as Minister of Personnel; Chongwang again as Director assisted the Southern Bureau and selections were handled clearly.
translations.idiomatic: When Anqian entered the capital as Minister of Personnel, Chongwang again headed the Southern Bureau as Director and handled selections with clarity.

sentences.zh: 僖宗幸山南，王重榮怨宦豎，不肯率職，時高選使者，即河中鐫諭使自新，崇望以諫議大夫持節往。

translations.literal: When Xizong journeyed south of the mountains Wang Chongrong resented the eunuchs and would not perform duty; at the time an envoy of high selection was needed; immediately at Hezhong he was engraved with instructions to persuade renewal; Chongwang went as Remonstrator with credentials.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong went south of the mountains, Wang Chongrong resented the eunuchs and refused to perform his duties; a high-ranking envoy was needed, and instructions were carved at Hezhong urging him to reform; Chongwang went as Remonstrating Censor with credentials.

sentences.zh: 既至，陳君臣大義動之，重榮順服，請誅硃玫自效。

translations.literal: On arrival he set forth the great righteousness of ruler and minister and moved him; Chongrong submitted and asked to execute Zhu Mei to prove his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he set forth the righteousness owed between ruler and minister and moved him; Chongrong submitted and offered to kill Zhu Mei to prove his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 使還，稱旨，擢翰林學士。

translations.literal: On return his service met approval and he was raised to Academician of the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned his mission pleased the throne and he was raised to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 昭宗即位，進中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong took the throne he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong took the throne he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Councilor.

sentences.zh: 張浚伐太原，崇望固執不可，浚果敗。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun campaigned against Taiyuan; Chongwang firmly opposed it and Jun was indeed defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jun campaigned against Taiyuan, Chongwang firmly opposed it, and Jun was indeed defeated.

sentences.zh: 代為門下侍郎、判度支。

translations.literal: He was replaced as Vice Director of the Gate and concurrently judged the Department of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was replaced as Vice Director of the Gate and put in charge of the Department of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 玉山都將楊守信反，夜陳兵闕下。

translations.literal: The Yushan commander's Yang Shouxin rebelled and by night arrayed troops below the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yushan commander Yang Shouxin rebelled and by night deployed troops below the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 帝列兵延喜門，命崇望守度支庫。

translations.literal: The emperor deployed troops at Yanxi Gate and ordered Chongwang to guard the revenue store.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor arrayed troops at Yanxi Gate and ordered Chongwang to guard the revenue treasury.

sentences.zh: 巉旦，含光門未開，禁卒左右植立，將大掠長安中。

translations.literal: At dawn Han guang Gate had not opened; guards stood left and right and were about to plunder greatly in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the Han guang Gate had not yet opened; palace guards stood on either side, about to loot Chang'an on a grand scale.

sentences.zh: 俄聞傳呼宰相來者，門辟，崇望駐馬勞曰：「上自將在中營，公等禁軍也，不帝前殺賊取功，而茍欲剽掠成惡名乎？」

translations.literal: Soon word passed that the chancellor was coming; the gate opened; Chongwang halted his horse and said in consolation: "The emperor himself leads from the central camp; you are the forbidden army — will you not kill the rebels before the emperor to win merit, but merely wish to plunder and earn an evil name?
translations.idiomatic: Soon a cry went up that the chancellor was coming; the gate opened; Chongwang reined in his horse and addressed them: "The emperor leads the central camp in person; you are the imperial guard—will you not kill the rebels before the emperor to win merit, but only loot and earn an evil name?

sentences.zh: 士皆唯唯。

translations.literal: The men all murmured assent.
translations.idiomatic: The men all murmured agreement.

sentences.zh: 至長樂門，賊望兵至，乃遁去，軍中咸呼「萬歲」。

translations.literal: Reaching Everlasting Joy Gate the rebels saw troops arrive and fled; the army all cried "Long live!"
translations.idiomatic: At Everlasting Joy Gate the rebels saw troops coming and fled; the whole army shouted "Long live!"

sentences.zh: 是日，京師不亂，繄其力。

translations.literal: That day the capital was not disturbed — it was owing to his force.
translations.idiomatic: That day the capital was not thrown into chaos—it was due to his effort.

sentences.zh: 進尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 硃全忠謀取徐、泗，表請以大臣代時溥，乃授崇望武寧軍節度使。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong plotted to take Xu and Si; memorial requested that a great minister replace Shi Pu; thereupon Chongwang was made Military Commissioner of Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong plotted to seize Xu and Si and memorialized that a senior minister replace Shi Pu; Chongwang was therefore made Military Commissioner of Wuning.

sentences.zh: 溥拒命，崇望還為太常卿。

translations.literal: Pu refused the order; Chongwang returned to be Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Pu refused the order, and Chongwang returned as Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 會王珂、王珙爭河中，詔以崔胤為節度使。

translations.literal: When Wang Ke and Wang Hong contended for Hezhong, an edict made Cui Yin military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ke and Wang Hong were fighting over Hezhong; the court appointed Cui Yin as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 珂，李克用婿也。

translations.literal: Ke was the son-in-law of Li Keyong.
translations.idiomatic: Ke was Li Keyong's son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 太原邸吏薛誌勤曰：「崔公鎮河中，不若光德劉公於我公最善。」

translations.literal: A Taiyuan lodge clerk Xue Zhiqin said: "If Lord Cui holds Hezhong, it is not as good as Lord Liu of Guangde, who is kindest to our lord.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk at Li Keyong's Taiyuan lodge, Xue Zhiqin, said: "If Lord Cui takes Hezhong, he is not as close to our lord as Lord Liu of Guangde.

sentences.zh: 光德，崇望所居坊也。

translations.literal: Guangde was the ward where Chongwang lived.
translations.idiomatic: Guangde was the ward where Chongwang lived.

sentences.zh: 後李茂貞、王行瑜入誅執政，坐是，貶昭州司馬。

translations.literal: Later Li Maozhen and Wang Xingyu entered the capital to kill the chief ministers; for this he was demoted to prefectural adjutant of Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Li Maozhen and Wang Xingyu entered the capital and killed the chief ministers, he was demoted to prefectural adjutant of Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 行瑜誅，克用直其冤，召為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Xingyu was executed, Keyong upheld his innocence and summoned him back as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingyu was killed, Keyong vindicated him and recalled him as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 會王摶以吏部輔政，徙兵部。

translations.literal: When Wang Tuan took the Ministry of Personnel to assist in government, Chongwang was moved to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Tuan joined the government as Minister of Personnel, Chongwang was transferred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 王建欲並東川，詔崇望為劍南東川節度使、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Wang Jian wished to annex Dongchuan; an edict made Chongwang Military Commissioner of Eastern Sword South and Concurrent Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian sought to annex Dongchuan; Chongwang was made Military Commissioner of Eastern Sword South and Concurrent Councilor.

sentences.zh: 未至，建已使王宗滌知留後，崇望乃還為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Jian had already sent Wang Zongdi to act as acting prefect; Chongwang therefore returned as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived, Jian had already sent Wang Zongdi to hold the post; Chongwang returned as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空。

translations.literal: On death he was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 崇望兄崇龜

translations.literal: Chongwang's elder brother Chonggui
translations.idiomatic: Chongwang's elder brother Chonggui

sentences.zh: 兄崇龜，字子長。

translations.literal: The elder brother Chonggui, styled Zichang.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Chonggui, styled Zichang.

sentences.zh: 擢進士，仕累華要，終清海軍節度使。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, served repeatedly in eminent posts, and ended as Military Commissioner of Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi, rose through important offices, and ended as Military Commissioner of Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 廣有大賈，約倡女夜集，而它盜殺女，遺刀去。

translations.literal: In Guang there was a great merchant who arranged to meet a singing girl at night, but another thief killed the girl and left the knife.
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy merchant in Guang arranged a night meeting with a courtesan, but another thief killed her and left the knife behind.

sentences.zh: 賈入倡家，踐其血乃覺，乘艑亡。

translations.literal: The merchant entered the house of entertainers, stepped in her blood and only then realized it, and fled in a small boat.
translations.idiomatic: The merchant entered the courtesan's house, stepped in blood, realized what had happened, and fled by boat.

sentences.zh: 吏跡賈捕劾，得約女狀而不殺也。

translations.literal: Officers traced the merchant and arrested him; they obtained the singing girl's testimony that he had not killed her.
translations.idiomatic: Officers tracked him down and arrested him; the courtesan's account showed he had not killed her.

sentences.zh: 崇龜方大饗軍中，悉集宰人，至日入，乃遣。

translations.literal: Chonggui was giving a great feast to the army and had gathered all the cooks; only at sunset did he dismiss them.
translations.idiomatic: Chonggui was hosting a great feast for the army and had all the cooks assembled; he dismissed them only at sunset.

sentences.zh: 陰以遺刀易一雜置之。

translations.literal: In secret he exchanged the abandoned knife for a kitchen knife and placed it among them.
translations.idiomatic: In secret he swapped the abandoned knife for a kitchen knife and mixed it in.

sentences.zh: 詰朝，群宰即庖取刀，一人不去，曰：「是非我刀。」

translations.literal: At dawn the cooks went to the kitchen for knives; one man would not leave and said: "This is not my knife.
translations.idiomatic: Next morning, as the cooks took knives from the kitchen, one refused to leave, saying: "This is not my knife.

sentences.zh: 問之，得其主名。

translations.literal: On questioning him they obtained the owner's name.
translations.idiomatic: Questioned, he gave the owner's name.

sentences.zh: 往視，則亡矣。

translations.literal: On going to look, the man was already gone.
translations.idiomatic: When they went to look, he had already fled.

sentences.zh: 崇龜取它囚殺之，聲言賈也，陳諸市。

translations.literal: Chonggui took another prisoner and executed him, proclaiming it was the merchant, and displayed him in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Chonggui executed another prisoner, announced it was the merchant, and displayed the body in the market.

sentences.zh: 亡宰歸，捕詰具伏。

translations.literal: The escaped cook returned; on arrest and interrogation he confessed fully.
translations.idiomatic: The escaped cook returned, was seized, and confessed everything.

sentences.zh: 其精明類此。

translations.literal: His keen discernment was of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His sharp discernment was of this kind.

sentences.zh: 姻舊或幹以財，率不答，但寫《荔支圖》與之。

translations.literal: When kin or friends asked him for money he generally refused, but only wrote out a Lychee Picture for them.
translations.idiomatic: When relatives or friends asked him for money he usually refused and only gave them a painting of lychees instead.

sentences.zh: 然不能防檢其家，既沒，有鬻珠翠羽者，由是名損。

translations.literal: Yet he could not keep watch over his household; after his death there were those who sold pearls and kingfisher feathers, and therefore his reputation suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he could not restrain his household; after his death some sold pearls and kingfisher ornaments, and his name was damaged.

sentences.zh: 崇望弟崇魯

translations.literal: Chongwang's younger brother Chonglu
translations.idiomatic: Chongwang's younger brother Chonglu

sentences.zh: 弟崇魯，字郊文，亦第進士，擢士補闕、翰林學士，僖宗避難山南，為嗣襄王煴史館修撰，得不誅。

translations.literal: The younger brother Chonglu, styled Jiaowen, also passed the jinshi, was raised to Supplementation Censor and Hanlin Academician; when Xizong fled south of the mountains he was historiographer for the heir Prince Yun and escaped execution.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Chonglu, styled Jiaowen, also passed the jinshi and rose to Supplementation Censor and Hanlin Academician; when Xizong fled south of the mountains he served as historiographer to the heir Prince Yun and was not executed.

sentences.zh: 景福中，以水部郎中知制誥。

translations.literal: In the Jingfu era he was Director of the Water Department with charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingfu era he was Director of the Water Department with charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 雅與崔昭緯善。

translations.literal: He was on close terms with Cui Zhaowei.
translations.idiomatic: He was on intimate terms with Cui Zhaowei.

sentences.zh: 帝以韋昭度、李磎輔政，而昭緯外倚邠、岐兵為援，以久其權。

translations.literal: The emperor made Wei Zhaodu and Li Xi chief ministers, while Zhaowei outwardly relied on the Bin and Qi armies as support to prolong his power.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Wei Zhaodu and Li Xi chief ministers, while Zhaowei relied outwardly on the Bin and Qi armies to prolong his power.

sentences.zh: 於是天子厚禮磎，昭緯懼見奪，共謀沮之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Son of Heaven richly honored Xi; Zhaowei feared being displaced and together plotted to obstruct him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then honored Xi generously; Zhaowei, fearing displacement, plotted with him to block Xi's appointment.

sentences.zh: 及磎墨麻出，崇魯輒掠麻大哭。

translations.literal: When Xi's black ink edict of appointment came out, Chonglu would seize the document and weep aloud.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi's appointment edict was issued, Chonglu would snatch the document and wail loudly.

sentences.zh: 帝問焉，崇魯曰：「今雖乏人，豈宜取憸人為宰相。

translations.literal: The emperor asked him; Chonglu said: "Though men are scarce today, how can we take a treacherous man as chancellor?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked why; Chonglu said: "Even if talent is scarce, how can we make a treacherous man chancellor?

sentences.zh: 磎以楊復恭、西門重遂得近職，奈何用之？

translations.literal: Xi gained his recent post through Yang Fugong and Ximen Chongsui — how can he be used?
translations.idiomatic: Xi got his recent post through Yang Fugong and Ximen Chongsui — how can we use him?

sentences.zh: 前日杜讓能羞戮未刷，尚忍蹈覆轍乎？」

translations.literal: The shame of Du Rangneng's death is not yet washed away — can we bear to tread the same path again?
translations.idiomatic: Du Rangneng's disgraceful death is not yet expunged — can we repeat that mistake?

sentences.zh: 磎由是不得相。

translations.literal: Xi therefore did not become chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Xi therefore did not become chancellor.

sentences.zh: 磎亦劾奏其奸，因自陳「為山南楊守亮詆毀，不容與復恭交私」。

translations.literal: Xi also memorialized accusing him of wickedness, and himself stated that "in the mountains south of the ranges Yang Shouliang slandered me, and I cannot be intimate with Fugong."
translations.idiomatic: Xi also memorialized accusing him of treachery, stating that "in the south Yang Shouliang slandered me, and I cannot be intimate with Fugong."

sentences.zh: 又言：「崇望為宰相，使親吏日夕謁左軍，與復恭相親厚。

translations.literal: He also said: "When Chongwang was chancellor he had a close clerk visit the Left Army daily and be intimate with Fugong.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "When Chongwang was chancellor his private clerk visited the Left Army daily and was close to Fugong.

sentences.zh: 絁巾慘帶，不入禁門；

translations.literal: Wearing silk headcloth and mourning sash, he would not enter the forbidden gate;
translations.idiomatic: Wearing a silk headcloth and mourning sash, he would not enter the forbidden gate;

sentences.zh: 崇魯向殿哭，厭詛天詐，殆人之妖。

translations.literal: Chonglu wept before the hall, cursing heaven's deceit — almost a human demon.
translations.idiomatic: Chonglu wept before the hall and cursed heaven's fraud — nearly a demon in human form.

sentences.zh: 且其父坐賄飲藥死。

translations.literal: Moreover his father died from taking poison after a bribery conviction.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover his father took poison after a bribery conviction.

sentences.zh: 崇魯身為硃玫史官，作勸進表。

translations.literal: Chonglu himself served Zhu Mei as historiographer and wrote the memorial urging enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: Chonglu himself was Zhu Mei's historiographer and wrote the memorial urging enthronement.

sentences.zh: 在太原府使西川，見田令孜，沒階趨，廢制度自崇魯始。」

translations.literal: At the Taiyuan office he was sent to the western circuit and, seeing Tian Lingzi, went down the steps in haste — the ruin of protocol began with Chonglu.
translations.idiomatic: Sent from Taiyuan to the western circuit, he saw Tian Lingzi and rushed down the steps — the collapse of court ritual began with Chonglu.

sentences.zh: 其相詈訾，俚淺稽校，譬市人然。

translations.literal: Their mutual reviling was vulgar and petty, like market folk.
translations.idiomatic: Their mutual abuse was vulgar and petty, like street traders.

sentences.zh: 崇龜始聞哭麻，恚不食。

translations.literal: When Chonggui first heard of the weeping over the edict, he was angry and would not eat.
translations.idiomatic: When Chonggui first heard of the weeping over the edict, he was furious and refused to eat.

sentences.zh: 曰：「吾兄弟未始以聲利敗名，今不幸乃生是兒。」

translations.literal: He said: "Our brothers have never ruined their names with clamor for profit; now unhappily this son was born.
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Our brothers never ruined our names chasing profit; now, unhappily, this son was born.

sentences.zh: 後王行瑜、崔昭緯相繼誅，崇魯貶崖州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Later Wang Xingyu and Cui Zhaowei were executed in succession; Chonglu was demoted to registrar of Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Xingyu and Cui Zhaowei were executed in turn; Chonglu was demoted to registrar of Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 終水部員外郎。

translations.literal: He ended as Director of the Water Department.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as Director of the Water Department.

sentences.zh: 許紹，字嗣宗，安州安陸人。

translations.literal: Xu Shao, styled Sizong, was a native of Anlu in An Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shao, styled Sizong, came from Anlu in An Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父法光，在隋為楚州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Faguang served the Sui as prefect of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Faguang had been prefect of Chu under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 元皇帝為安州總管，紹時為兒，與高祖同學，相愛也。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yuan was Grand Protector of An Prefecture, Shao was still a boy and studied with Gaozu; they loved each other.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yuan was Grand Protector of An, Shao was still a boy and studied with the future Gaozu; they were fond of each other.

sentences.zh: 大業末，任夷陵通守，會盜起，州境獨完，流人自占數十萬，開倉賑給。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he was transit governor of Yiling; when bandits rose his prefecture alone remained intact, and refugees numbering hundreds of thousands attached themselves; he opened the granaries to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Daye he was transit governor of Yiling; when bandits rose his district alone stayed intact, and hundreds of thousands of refugees gathered; he opened the granaries to feed them.

sentences.zh: 煬帝崩問至，紹率人吏三日臨，以所部遙屬越王侗。

translations.literal: When news of Emperor Yang's death arrived, Shao led officials and people in three days of mourning and from his command remotely submitted to Prince Tong of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When news of Yang's death arrived, Shao led officials and people in mourning for three days and submitted his district to Prince Tong of Yue.

sentences.zh: 後王世充篡立，遂遣使以黔安、武陵、澧陽歸國，授峽州刺史，封安陸郡公。

translations.literal: Later when Wang Shichong usurped the throne he sent envoys to offer Qian'an, Wuling, and Liyang to the Tang, and was made prefect of Xia and enfeoffed Duke of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Wang Shichong seized the throne, he sent envoys offering Qian'an, Wuling, and Liyang to the Tang and was made prefect of Xia and enfeoffed Duke of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 高祖賜書道平生舊，以加慰納。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent a letter recalling their old friendship to comfort and win him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu wrote recalling their old friendship to comfort and win him over.

sentences.zh: 蕭銑將董景珍降，命紹率兵應接。

translations.literal: When Xiao Xian's general Dong Jingzhen surrendered, he ordered Shao to lead troops to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Xian's general Dong Jingzhen surrendered, Shao was ordered to lead troops to receive him.

sentences.zh: 以破銑功，擢其子智仁為溫州刺史。

translations.literal: For the merit in defeating Xian, his son Zhiren was raised to prefect of Wen.
translations.idiomatic: For defeating Xian, his son Zhiren was made prefect of Wen.

sentences.zh: 銑遣楊道生圍峽州，紹擊走之。

translations.literal: Xian sent Yang Daosheng to besiege Xia Prefecture; Shao attacked and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Xian sent Yang Daosheng to besiege Xia; Shao attacked and repelled him.

sentences.zh: 銑將陳普環具大艦溯江，與開州賊蕭阇提略巴、蜀，紹遣智仁及婿張玄靖、掾李弘節追戰西陵，覆其兵，禽普環，悉獲戰艦。

translations.literal: Xian's general Chen Puhuan brought great ships up the river with Xiao Sheti of Kaizhou to raid Ba and Shu; Shao sent Zhiren, his son-in-law Zhang Xuanjing, and aide Li Hongjie to pursue and fight at Xiling, overturned his force, captured Puhuan, and took all the warships.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's general Chen Puhuan sailed upriver with great ships, together with Kaizhou's Xiao Sheti raiding Ba and Shu; Shao sent Zhiren, his son-in-law Zhang Xuanjing, and aide Li Hongjie to fight at Xiling, destroyed the force, captured Puhuan, and seized all the warships.

sentences.zh: 江之南有安蜀城，地直夷陵，荊門城峙其東，皆峭險處。

translations.literal: South of the river was Fortress Pacify Shu, directly facing Yiling, with Jingmen Fortress towering to its east — all precipitous places.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river stood Fortress Pacify Shu facing Yiling, with Jingmen Fortress looming to the east — all steep strongpoints.

sentences.zh: 銑以兵戍守，紹遣智仁等攻荊門，取之。

translations.literal: Xian garrisoned troops there; Shao sent Zhiren and others to attack Jingmen and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Xian stationed troops there; Shao sent Zhiren and others to attack Jingmen and captured it.

sentences.zh: 制書褒美，許以便宜。

translations.literal: An edict praised him and permitted discretionary action.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised him and allowed discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 紹境連王世充及銑，其下為賊剽者皆見殺，紹得敵人，獨資遣之，二邦感義，殺掠為止。

translations.literal: Shao's territory bordered Wang Shichong and Xian; his subordinates who plundered as bandits were all executed, but enemies he captured he alone supplied and sent away; the two states were moved by righteousness and killing and plunder ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's territory bordered Shichong and Xian; subordinates who robbed as bandits he executed, but captives he supplied and released; both states were moved by his righteousness and raids stopped.

sentences.zh: 進譙國公，賜帛千段。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Duke of Qiao and given a thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Duke of Qiao and given a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 趙郡王孝恭等代銑，復詔督兵圖荊州。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Zhao Li Xiaogong and others replaced Xian, another edict ordered him to supervise troops against Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Zhao Li Xiaogong and others replaced Xian, he was again ordered to direct troops against Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 會病，卒於軍，帝為流涕。

translations.literal: He fell ill and died in the army; the emperor wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and died in camp; the emperor wept for him.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，贈荊州都督。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan he was posthumously made Governor of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan he was posthumously made Governor of Jing.

sentences.zh: 智仁，初以勛授封孝昌縣公，紹卒，繼守夷陵，終涼州都督。

translations.literal: Zhiren at first received his fief through merit as Duke of Xiaochang; when Shao died he continued to guard Yiling and ended as Governor of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiren first received the fief of Xiaochang through merit; when Shao died he continued guarding Yiling and ended as Governor of Liang.

sentences.zh: 次子圉師。

translations.literal: The second son Tushi.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Tushi.

sentences.zh: 圉師有器幹，研涉藝文，擢進士第。

translations.literal: Tushi had capacity and resolve, studied the arts and letters, and passed the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Tushi had ability and breadth, studied literature, and passed the jinshi.

sentences.zh: 累遷給事中、黃門侍郎、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Supervising Censor, Vice Director of the Gate, and Third Rank Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Supervising Censor, Vice Director of the Gate, and Third Rank Councilor.

sentences.zh: 龍朔中，為左相。

translations.literal: In the Longshuo era he was Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Longshuo era he was Left Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 高宗自書詔賜遼東諸將，謂許敬宗曰：「圉師愛書，可示之。」

translations.literal: Gaozong himself wrote an edict for the generals of Liaodong and told Xu Jingzong: "Tushi loves books — you may show it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong wrote in his own hand an edict for the Liaodong generals and told Xu Jingzong: "Tushi loves books — show it to him.

sentences.zh: 俄坐其子獵犯人田，有辭，怒而射之，圉師掩不奏，為人告擿。

translations.literal: Before long, because his son hunted and trespassed on another's field and quarreled, he angrily shot the man; Tushi concealed it and did not memorialize, and someone reported and exposed it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his son hunted on another man's land, quarreled, and Tushi angrily shot the man; Tushi concealed it and did not report it, and someone exposed him.

sentences.zh: 帝讓曰：「宰相而暴百姓，非作威福乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor reproved him: "A chancellor who brutalizes the people — is this not making a display of power?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reproved him: "A chancellor who brutalizes the people — is that not lording power over them?

sentences.zh: 圉師謝，且言：「作威福者，強兵重鎮，嫚天子法。

translations.literal: Tushi apologized and said: "Those who make a display of power are strong armies and heavy garrisons that scorn the Son of Heaven's law.
translations.idiomatic: Tushi apologized and said: "Those who lord power are great armies and heavy commands that despise imperial law.

sentences.zh: 臣文吏，何敢然！」

translations.literal: I am a civil official — how would I dare!"
translations.idiomatic: I am a civil official — how would I dare!"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「慊無兵邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Do you begrudge having no troops?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Do you mean you have no troops?"

sentences.zh: 敬宗因是劾抵，遂免官。

translations.literal: Jingzong therefore used this to impeach and press charges, and he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong seized on this to impeach him, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 久之，為虔州刺史，稍遷相州，專以寬治，州人刻石頌美。

translations.literal: After a long while he was prefect of Qian, then gradually transferred to Xiang, governing exclusively with leniency; the people carved stone to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was prefect of Qian, then of Xiang, governing with leniency; the people set up a stone to praise him.

sentences.zh: 部有受賕者，圉師不忍按，但賜《清白箴》，其人自愧，後修飾，更為廉士。

translations.literal: In his department someone took bribes; Tushi could not bear to prosecute him but only gave him the Admonition on Integrity; the man was ashamed, later reformed himself, and became an upright man.
translations.idiomatic: Someone in his department took bribes; Tushi could not bear to prosecute him but gave him the Admonition on Integrity; the man was ashamed, reformed, and became upright.

sentences.zh: 進戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Minister of the People.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Minister of the People.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈幽州都督，謚曰簡，陪葬恭陵。

translations.literal: On death he was posthumously made Governor of You with posthumous title Jian and buried beside Gongling.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Governor of You with posthumous title Jian and buried beside Gongling.

sentences.zh: 紹初爵譙國公，以子智仁自有封，故詔孫力士襲之，終洛州長史。

translations.literal: Shao was first enfeoffed Duke of Qiao; because his son Zhiren already had a fief, an edict had his grandson Lishi inherit it; Lishi ended as prefectural secretary of Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was first Duke of Qiao; because Zhiren already had a fief, an edict had grandson Lishi inherit; Lishi ended as secretary of Luo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 子欽寂

translations.literal: The son Qinji
translations.idiomatic: The son Qinji

sentences.zh: 欽寂弟欽明

translations.literal: Qinji's younger brother Qinming
translations.idiomatic: Qinji's younger brother Qinming

sentences.zh: 欽寂弟欽明，以軍功擢左玉鈐衛將軍、安西大都護、鹽山郡公。

translations.literal: Qinji's younger brother Qinming, through military merit was raised to General of the Left Jade Bell Guard, Grand Protector of Anxi, and Duke of Yanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Qinming, younger brother of Qinji, through military merit became General of the Left Jade Bell Guard, Grand Protector of Anxi, and Duke of Yanshan.

sentences.zh: 出為涼州都督。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Governor of Liang.

sentences.zh: 嘗輕騎按部，會突厥默啜兵奄至，被執。

translations.literal: Once on light horse he inspected his district; Mohe soldiers of the Turks suddenly arrived and he was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Once while inspecting lightly mounted, the Turk Mohe's troops suddenly arrived and seized him.

sentences.zh: 賊與皆至靈州，使說之降。

translations.literal: The bandits took him all to Ling Prefecture and made him urge surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits brought him to Ling Prefecture and made him urge surrender.

sentences.zh: 欽明至城下，呼曰：「我乏食，有美醬乎？

translations.literal: Qinming came below the wall and called: "I lack food — do you have fine sauce?
translations.idiomatic: Qinming came to the foot of the wall and shouted: "I have no food — do you have good sauce?

sentences.zh: 有粱米乎？

translations.literal: Do you have millet?
translations.idiomatic: Do you have millet?

sentences.zh: 並乞墨一枝！」

translations.literal: And beg one stick of ink!
translations.idiomatic: And lend me one stick of ink!

sentences.zh: 時賊營四面阻水，惟一路得入。

translations.literal: At the time the bandit camp was blocked by water on four sides; only one road allowed entry.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit camp was surrounded by water on four sides; only one road led in.

sentences.zh: 欽明欲選將簡兵，乘夜襲賊也，而城中無寤其瘦者，遂見害。

translations.literal: Qinming wished to choose a general and elite troops to strike the bandits by night, but those in the city did not grasp his subtlety and he was therefore killed.
translations.idiomatic: Qinming meant to choose a general and crack troops for a night raid, but the city did not understand his subtlety and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 兄弟死王事，世名其忠。

translations.literal: The brothers died in the king's service; the age names them loyal.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers died in the ruler's service; the age calls them loyal.

sentences.zh: 程知節

translations.literal: Cheng Zhijie
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Zhijie

sentences.zh: 程知節本名咬金，濟州東阿人。

translations.literal: Cheng Zhijie, original name Yaojin, was a native of Dong'e in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Zhijie, born Yaojin, came from Dong'e in Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 善馬槊。

translations.literal: He was skilled with the horse lance.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled with the cavalry lance.

sentences.zh: 隋末，所在盜起，知節聚眾數百保鄉里。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui bandits rose everywhere; Zhijie gathered several hundred men to protect his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Sui, when bandits rose everywhere, Zhijie gathered several hundred men to defend his home district.

sentences.zh: 後事李密，而密料士八千隸四驃騎，分左右以自衛，號「內軍」，常曰：「此可當百萬。」

translations.literal: Later he served Li Mi, and Mi selected eight thousand elite troops for four Swift Cavalry commands, divided left and right for his own guard, called the "Inner Army"; he often said: "These can match a million."
translations.idiomatic: Later he served Li Mi, who picked eight thousand elite troops for four Swift Cavalry commands as his personal guard, the "Inner Army"; Mi often said they were worth a million men.

sentences.zh: 知節領驃騎之一，恩遇隆特。

translations.literal: Zhijie commanded one of the Swift Cavalry units and received exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijie led one Swift Cavalry unit and was favored exceptionally.

sentences.zh: 王世充與密戰，知節以內騎營北邙，單雄信以外騎營偃師。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong fought Mi; Zhijie with the inner cavalry camp was at Beimang, and Shan Xiongxin with the outer cavalry camp at Yanshi.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong fought Mi, Zhijie's inner cavalry camp was at Beimang and Shan Xiongxin's outer camp at Yanshi.

sentences.zh: 世充襲雄信，密遣知節及裴行儼助之。

translations.literal: Shichong attacked Xiongxin; Mi sent Zhijie and Pei Xingyan to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong attacked Xiongxin; Mi sent Zhijie and Pei Xingyan to help.

sentences.zh: 行儼中流矢墜馬，知節馳救之，殺數人，軍辟易，乃抱行儼重騎馳。

translations.literal: Xingyan was struck by an arrow and fell from his horse; Zhijie galloped to rescue him, killed several men, the army gave way, and he lifted Xingyan back onto a horse and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyan took an arrow and fell; Zhijie charged to save him, killed several men, forced the enemy aside, lifted Xingyan onto a horse, and rode off.

sentences.zh: 追兵以槊撞之，知節折其槊，斬追者，乃免。

translations.literal: Pursuers struck him with lances; Zhijie broke their lances, cut down the pursuers, and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuers struck with lances; he broke the lances, killed the pursuers, and got away.

sentences.zh: 後密敗，為世充所獲。

translations.literal: Later Mi was defeated and he was captured by Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi was defeated he was taken by Shichong.

sentences.zh: 惡其為人，與秦叔寶來奔，授秦王府左三統軍。

translations.literal: He detested Shichong's conduct and came over with Qin Shubao; he was made Left Third Commander of the Prince of Qin's household.
translations.idiomatic: Disliking Shichong, he fled with Qin Shubao and was made Left Third Commander of the Qin princely household.

sentences.zh: 從破宋金剛、竇建德、王世充，並領左一馬軍總管，搴旗先登者不一，以功封宿國公。

translations.literal: He followed in defeating Song Jingang, Dou Jiande, and Wang Shichong, and each time commanded the Left First Horse Army; he seized banners and led the charge more than once, and for merit was enfeoffed Duke of Su.
translations.idiomatic: He helped defeat Song Jingang, Dou Jiande, and Wang Shichong, repeatedly commanding the Left First Horse Army, seizing banners and charging first, and was enfeoffed Duke of Su.

sentences.zh: 七年，隱太子譖之，出為康州刺史，白秦王曰：「大王去左右手矣，身欲久全，得乎？

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Hidden Crown Prince slandered him and he was sent out as prefect of Kang; he told the Prince of Qin: "Your Highness has lost your left and right hands — can you long preserve yourself?
translations.idiomatic: In year seven the Hidden Crown Prince slandered him and he was posted to Kang; he told the Prince of Qin: "You have lost your right and left hands — can you long remain safe?

sentences.zh: 知節有死，不敢去！」

translations.literal: Zhijie would die — he dared not leave!
translations.idiomatic: Zhijie would die before he would leave!

sentences.zh: 事平，拜太子右衛率。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was made Right Guard of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: After the affair was settled he was made Right Guard of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 尋遷右武衛大將軍，實封七百戶。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guard with a substantive fief of seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guard with seven hundred substantive households.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，歷瀘州都督、左領軍大將軍，改封盧國。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan he served as Governor of Lu and Left Commander-in-Chief, and his fief was changed to the state of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan he was Governor of Lu and Left Commander-in-Chief, and his fief became the state of Lu.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年，授蔥山道行軍大總管，以討賀魯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianqing he was made Grand Commander of the Onion Mountain campaign to attack Helu.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing year two he was Grand Commander of the Onion Mountain campaign against Helu.

sentences.zh: 師次怛篤城，胡人數千出降，知節屠其城去，賀魯因遠遁。

translations.literal: When the army reached Dudu City several thousand barbarians came out to surrender; Zhijie slaughtered the city and left, and Helu therefore fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: At Dudu City thousands of barbarians surrendered; Zhijie massacred the city and withdrew, and Helu fled far away.

sentences.zh: 軍還，坐免。

translations.literal: On the army's return he was dismissed for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was dismissed for it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，起為岐州刺史，致仕。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled as prefect of Qi and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as prefect of Qi and retired.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈驃騎大將軍、益州大都督，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: On death he was posthumously made General-in-Chief of Swift Cavalry and Grand Protector of Yi and buried beside Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made General-in-Chief of Swift Cavalry and Grand Protector of Yi, buried beside Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 子處亮，尚清河公主。

translations.literal: His son Chuliang married the Princess of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chuliang married the Princess of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 柴紹，字嗣昌，晉州臨汾人。

translations.literal: Chai Shao, styled Sichang, was a native of Linfen in Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Shao, styled Sichang, came from Linfen in Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼矯悍，有武力，以任俠聞。

translations.literal: In youth he was fierce and had martial strength, known for chivalrous deeds.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was fierce and strong, famed for chivalry.

sentences.zh: 補隋太子千牛備身。

translations.literal: He entered service as a Thousand-Ox Attendant of the Sui crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Thousand-Ox Attendant to the Sui crown prince.

sentences.zh: 高祖妻以平陽公主。

translations.literal: Gaozu gave him the Princess of Pingyang in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu married him to the Princess of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 將起兵，紹走間道迎謁。

translations.literal: When they were about to raise the army Shao went by a hidden route to meet and pay homage.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising was planned Shao took a hidden route to join them.

sentences.zh: 時太子建成、齊王元吉亦自河東往，遇諸塗。

translations.literal: At the time the crown prince Jiancheng and Prince of Qi Yuanji also came from Hedong and met them on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince Jiancheng and Prince of Qi Yuanji were also coming from Hedong and met them on the road.

sentences.zh: 建成曰：「追書急，恐吏逮捕，請依劇賊，冀自全。」

translations.literal: Jiancheng said: "The urgent pursuit letter is pressing; I fear officials will arrest us — let us join fierce bandits, hoping to save ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng said: "Pursuit is urgent and officials may arrest us — let us join fierce bandits to save ourselves.

sentences.zh: 紹曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Shao said: "That will not do.
translations.idiomatic: Shao said: "That will not do.

sentences.zh: 賊知君唐公子，必執以為功，徒死爾。

translations.literal: Bandits will know you are Tang princes and surely seize you for merit — you will die for nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits will know you are Tang princes and seize you for reward — you will die for nothing.

sentences.zh: 不如疾走太原。」

translations.literal: Better hurry to Taiyuan."
translations.idiomatic: Better hurry to Taiyuan."

sentences.zh: 既入雀鼠谷，聞義兵起，謂紹有謀，乃相賀。

translations.literal: Once they entered Sparrow-Rat Valley and heard the righteous army had risen, they told Shao he had planned it and congratulated each other.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Sparrow-Rat Valley they heard the uprising had begun, thought Shao had planned it, and congratulated one another.

sentences.zh: 授右領軍大都督府長史，領彀騎，發晉陽。

translations.literal: He was made chief clerk of the Right Commander-in-Chief's Office, commanding Garrison Cavalry, and set out from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief clerk of the Right Commander-in-Chief's office, led Garrison Cavalry, and marched from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 先抵霍邑城下，覘形勢。

translations.literal: He first reached below Huoyi city and reconnoitered the situation.
translations.idiomatic: He first reached Huoyi and reconnoitered.

sentences.zh: 還白：「宋老生一夫敵，我兵到必出戰，可虜也。」

translations.literal: Returning he reported: "Song Laosheng is a single foe; when our army arrives he is sure to come out and fight — we can capture him.
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "Song Laosheng is alone in command; when our army comes he will fight and we can take him.

sentences.zh: 大師至，老生果出，紹力戰有功。

translations.literal: When the great army arrived Laosheng indeed came out; Shao fought hard with merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army came Laosheng did come out; Shao fought with merit.

sentences.zh: 從下臨汾、絳郡，隋將桑顯和來戰，紹引軍繚其背，與史大奈合攻之。

translations.literal: Following the capture of Linfen and Jiang Commandery, Sui general Sang Xianhe came to fight; Shao led troops around his rear and joined Shi Danae in attack.
translations.idiomatic: In taking Linfen and Jiang, Sui general Sang Xianhe attacked; Shao circled his rear and with Shi Danae struck him.

sentences.zh: 顯和敗，遂平京師。

translations.literal: Xianhe was defeated and the capital was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Xianhe was defeated and the capital was secured.

sentences.zh: 進右光祿大夫，封臨汾郡公。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed Duke of Linfen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Duke of Linfen.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，拜左翊衛大將軍，累從征討，以多，進封霍國公，遷右驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne he was made General-in-Chief of the Left Wing Guard; he followed repeatedly on campaigns and for many merits was advanced to Duke of Huo and transferred to General-in-Chief of the Right Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaozu's accession he was General-in-Chief of the Left Wing Guard; on many campaigns he was advanced to Duke of Huo and made General-in-Chief of the Right Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾、党項寇邊，敕紹討之，虜據高射紹軍，雨矢，士失色。

translations.literal: When Tuyuhun and the Tangut raided the border, Shao was ordered to attack; the barbarians held the heights and shot down on Shao's army; arrows fell like rain and the soldiers lost color.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuyuhun and Tangut raided the frontier, Shao attacked; the enemy held high ground and rained arrows; the troops blanched.

sentences.zh: 紹安坐，遣人彈胡琵琶，使二女子舞。

translations.literal: Shao sat at ease and had someone play the barbarian pipa while two women danced.
translations.idiomatic: Shao sat calmly, had someone play the Kuchean pipa, and set two women dancing.

sentences.zh: 虜疑之，休射觀。

translations.literal: The barbarians suspected this and ceased shooting to watch.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians were puzzled, stopped shooting, and watched.

sentences.zh: 紹伺其懈，以精騎從後掩擊，虜大潰，斬首五百級。

translations.literal: Shao waited until they slackened and with crack cavalry struck from behind; the barbarians were utterly routed and five hundred heads were cut.
translations.idiomatic: When they relaxed he struck from the rear with elite cavalry; the enemy fled in rout and five hundred heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，平梁師都，轉左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan he pacified Liang Shidu and was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan year two he pacified Liang Shidu and became General-in-Chief of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 出為華州刺史，加鎮軍大將軍，徙譙國。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Hua, was made Mighty General Who Guards the Army, and his fief was moved to Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: He became prefect of Hua, Mighty General Who Guards the Army, and his fief moved to Qiao.

sentences.zh: 既病，太宗親問之。

translations.literal: When he fell ill Taizong visited him in person.
translations.idiomatic: When ill Taizong visited him personally.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈荊州都督，謚曰襄。

translations.literal: On death he was posthumously made Governor of Jing with posthumous title Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously Governor of Jing with posthumous title Xiang.

sentences.zh: 二子：哲威、令武。

translations.literal: Two sons: Zhewei and Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Zhewei and Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 哲威為右屯衛將軍，襲封。

translations.literal: Zhewei was General of the Right Encampment Guard and inherited the fief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhewei was General of the Right Encampment Guard and inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 坐弟謀反，免死，流邵州。

translations.literal: For his younger brother's rebellion he was spared death and exiled to Shao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For his brother's rebellion he was spared death and exiled to Shao.

sentences.zh: 起為交州都督，卒。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Governor of Jiaozhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Governor of Jiaozhou and died.

sentences.zh: 令武尚巴陵公主，遷太僕少卿、衛州刺史、襄陽郡公。

translations.literal: Lingwu married the Princess of Baling, was made Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, prefect of Wei, and Duke of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lingwu married the Princess of Baling, became Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud, prefect of Wei, and Duke of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 與房遺愛謀反，貶嵐州刺史，自殺。

translations.literal: For plotting rebellion with Fang Yiai he was demoted to prefect of Lan and committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: For plotting with Fang Yiai he was demoted to Lan and killed himself.

sentences.zh: 公主亦賜死。

translations.literal: The princess was also ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was also ordered to die.

sentences.zh: 任瑰，字瑋，廬州合淝人。

translations.literal: Ren Gui, styled Wei, was a native of Hefei in Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Gui, styled Wei, came from Hefei in Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父七寶，陳將忠之弟，為陳定遠太守。

translations.literal: His father Qibao was younger brother of Chen general Ren Zhong and was Chen's prefect of Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qibao was younger brother of Chen general Ren Zhong and Chen prefect of Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 瑰早孤，忠撫愛甚，每曰：「吾子雖多，庸保耳。

translations.literal: Gui was orphaned early; Zhong loved and nurtured him greatly and often said: "Though I have many sons, they are mere hirelings.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was orphaned young; Zhong cherished him and often said: "I have many sons, but they are mere hirelings.

sentences.zh: 所以寄門戶者，瑰也！」

translations.literal: The one I entrust with the family gate is Gui!
translations.idiomatic: The one I trust with the house is Gui!

sentences.zh: 年十九，試守靈溪令。

translations.literal: At nineteen he was tried as acting magistrate of Lingxi.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he served as acting magistrate of Lingxi.

sentences.zh: 遷衡州司馬，都督王勇盡以州務屬瑰。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military adjutant of Heng Prefecture; Protector Wang Yong entrusted all prefectural affairs to Gui.
translations.idiomatic: He became adjutant of Heng; Protector Wang Yong gave him all prefectural business.

sentences.zh: 陳亡，瑰勸勇據嶺外，立陳後輔之。

translations.literal: When Chen fell Gui urged Yong to hold the region beyond the mountains and set up a Chen heir to assist.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell Gui urged Yong to hold the far south and install a Chen heir.

sentences.zh: 勇不從，以地降隋，瑰棄官去。

translations.literal: Yong would not follow and surrendered the territory to Sui; Gui abandoned office and left.
translations.idiomatic: Yong refused and surrendered to Sui; Gui quit his post and left.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，調韓城尉，未幾，罷。

translations.literal: In Renshou he was assigned as aide of Hancheng and soon left office.
translations.idiomatic: In Renshou he was aide of Hancheng and soon left.

sentences.zh: 高祖討捕於汾、晉，瑰上謁轅門，承制署河東縣戶曹。

translations.literal: When Gaozu pursued bandits in Fen and Jin, Gui presented himself at the camp gate and was appointed by provisional order as Household Registrar of Hedong County.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu campaigned in Fen and Jin, Gui came to the camp and was made Hedong County Household Registrar.

sentences.zh: 高祖之晉陽，留隱太子托之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu went to Jinyang he left the Hidden Crown Prince in Gui's care.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu went to Jinyang he entrusted the Hidden Crown Prince to Gui.

sentences.zh: 義師起，瑰至龍門請見。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose Gui came to Longmen to request audience.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising began Gui came to Longmen to see him.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「隋失其政，四海群沸，吾以外戚據重任，不忍坐觀其亡。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "The Sui have lost the Way and the four seas boil; as an imperial in-law holding heavy office I cannot sit and watch its fall.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said: "Sui has lost the Way and the realm boils; as an imperial in-law in heavy office I cannot watch it fall.

sentences.zh: 晉陽，天下用武處，兵精馬強，今率之，將厭國難。

translations.literal: Jinyang is where the realm uses arms — troops refined and horses strong; leading them now, we will satisfy the nation's distress.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyang is the realm's martial center — troops and horses are strong; leading them we can end the crisis.

sentences.zh: 公，將家子，智算練達，論吾此舉其濟乎？」

translations.literal: You are a general's son, skilled in calculation — will my undertaking succeed?
translations.idiomatic: You are a general's son, shrewd in counsel — will this succeed?

sentences.zh: 瑰曰：「今主政殘酷，兵役不止，天下之人，思見拯亂，與之息肩。

translations.literal: Gui said: "Today the ruler's government is cruel and military service unceasing; all under heaven long to be saved from chaos and to rest their shoulders.
translations.idiomatic: Gui said: "The throne is cruel and conscription endless; the people long for deliverance.

sentences.zh: 公天付神武，杖順而起，軍令嚴明，所下城邑，無秋豪之犯。

translations.literal: Your Grace is heaven-endowed with divine martial prowess, rising with the righteous cause; army orders are strict and cities taken suffer not the slightest harm.
translations.idiomatic: You rise with heaven's mandate and righteous arms; discipline is strict and no city you take suffers harm.

sentences.zh: 關中起兵者跂踵而待。

translations.literal: Those who rise in Guanzhong wait heel to toe.
translations.idiomatic: Forces in Guanzhong wait eagerly.

sentences.zh: 擁義師，迎眾欲，何不濟哉！

translations.literal: Uphold the righteous army and meet the people's desire — how would it not succeed!
translations.idiomatic: Lead the righteous army and the people's wish — how could you fail?

sentences.zh: 瑰在馮翊久，悉其人情，願為一介使，入關宣布威靈，以收左輔。

translations.literal: Gui has long been in Fengyi and knows its human feelings; he wishes to be a single envoy entering the passes to proclaim your majesty and gather the left flank.
translations.idiomatic: Gui knows Fengyi well and asks to go alone into the passes to proclaim your power and win the left flank.

sentences.zh: 繇梁山濟河，直趣韓城，逼郃陽，徇朝邑。

translations.literal: Cross the river by way of Liang Mountain, go straight to Hancheng, press Heyang, and sweep Chaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Cross at Liang Mountain, strike Hancheng, press Heyang, and take Chaoyi.

sentences.zh: 蕭造文吏，勢當自下。

translations.literal: Xiao Zao is a civil clerk — his force is sure to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zao is a civil official — he will submit.

sentences.zh: 次招諸賊，然後鼓行而前，據永豐積粟，雖未得京師，關中固已定矣。」

translations.literal: Next summon the other bandits, then advance with drums; hold the Yongfeng granary — though the capital is not yet taken, Guanzhong is already secured."
translations.idiomatic: Then win the other bandits, advance, hold Yongfeng's grain — even without the capital, Guanzhong is secured."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「是吾心也！」

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "That is my own heart!"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said: "That is exactly my mind!"

sentences.zh: 乃授銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with silver seal.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with silver seal.

sentences.zh: 遣陳演壽、史大奈步騎六千趣梁山，以瑰及薛獻為招慰大使。

translations.literal: He sent Chen Yanshou and Shi Danae with six thousand foot and horse toward Liang Mountain, with Gui and Xue Xian as envoys to comfort and summon.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Chen Yanshou and Shi Danae with six thousand troops toward Liang Mountain, with Gui and Xue Xian as envoys.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂演壽曰：「閫外事與任瑰籌之。」

translations.literal: Gaozu told Yanshou: "Matters outside the gate — plan them with Ren Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu told Yanshou: "Outside affairs — consult Ren Gui.

sentences.zh: 既而賊孫華、白玄度等果降，且具舟於河以濟師。

translations.literal: Before long bandits Sun Hua, Bai Xuandu, and others did submit and prepared boats on the river to ferry the army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Sun Hua, Bai Xuandu, and others submitted and prepared boats to ferry the army.

sentences.zh: 瑰行說下韓城，與諸將進擊飲馬泉，破之。

translations.literal: Gui went to win over Hancheng and with the generals advanced to attack Drinking-Horse Spring and defeated it.
