translations.idiomatic: Gui won Hancheng and with the generals attacked Drinking-Horse Spring and won.

sentences.zh: 拜左光祿大夫，留戍永豐倉。

translations.literal: He was made Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and left to guard Yongfeng granary.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and guarded Yongfeng granary.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，授谷州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne he was made prefect of Gu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaozu's accession he was prefect of Gu.

sentences.zh: 王世充數攻新安，瑰拒破之。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong repeatedly attacked Xin'an; Gui repelled and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong repeatedly attacked Xin'an; Gui repelled him.

sentences.zh: 以功封管國公。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Guan.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Guan.

sentences.zh: 秦王東討，瑰從至邙山，主水運餉軍。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qin campaigned east he followed to Mount Mang and directed water transport to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qin marched east Gui followed to Mount Mang and supplied the army by water.

sentences.zh: 關東平，為河南安撫大使。

translations.literal: When the east was pacified he was made Pacification Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When the east was pacified he was Pacification Commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 王世辯以徐州降瑰，瑰至宋州，會徐圓朗反，副使柳浚勸退保汴，瑰笑曰：「公何怯？

translations.literal: Wang Shibian surrendered Xuzhou to Gui; Gui reached Song Prefecture when Xu Yuanlang rebelled; Vice Commissioner Liu Jun urged retreat to Bian; Gui laughed: "Sir, how timid!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shibian surrendered Xuzhou; at Song, Xu Yuanlang rebelled; Liu Jun urged retreat to Bian; Gui laughed: "How timid you are!

sentences.zh: 老將居邊久，自當有計。」

translations.literal: An old general long on the frontier surely has a plan.
translations.idiomatic: An old frontier general surely has a plan.

sentences.zh: 俄而賊陷楚丘，將圍虞城，瑰遣崔樞、張公謹自鄢陵領諸州豪質子百餘守之。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits took Chuqiu and were about to besiege Yucheng; Gui sent Cui Shu and Zhang Gongjin from Yanling with more than a hundred hostages from prefectural magnates to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels took Chuqiu and besieged Yucheng; Gui sent Cui Shu and Zhang Gongjin with over a hundred magnates' sons as hostages to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 浚曰：「樞等故世充將，且諸州質子父兄皆反，奈何令保城？」

translations.literal: Jun said: "Shu and the rest were formerly Shichong's generals, and the hostages' fathers and brothers have all rebelled — how can you have them hold the city?
translations.idiomatic: Jun said: "Shu was Shichong's man, and the hostages' kin have rebelled — how can they hold the city?

sentences.zh: 瑰不答。

translations.literal: Gui did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Gui did not answer.

sentences.zh: 樞至，則分質子與土人合隊，賊近，質子稍叛，樞即斬其隊帥。

translations.literal: When Shu arrived he mixed hostages with locals in companies; as bandits neared some hostages wavered and Shu beheaded their captains.
translations.idiomatic: Shu mixed hostages with locals; when rebels neared some wavered and Shu killed their captains.

sentences.zh: 城中人懼曰：「是皆賊子弟，安可與守乎？」

translations.literal: The people in the city feared: "These are all bandits' sons — how can we defend with them?
translations.idiomatic: The townspeople feared: "These are bandits' sons — how can we defend with them?

sentences.zh: 樞因聽諸隊殺質子，梟首門外。

translations.literal: Shu therefore allowed each company to kill its hostages and display the heads outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Shu let each company kill its hostages and hung the heads outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 瑰陽怒曰：「去者遣招慰，何乃殺之？」

translations.literal: Gui pretended anger: "I sent them to win people over — why kill them?
translations.idiomatic: Gui feigned anger: "I sent them to win people — why kill them?

sentences.zh: 退謂浚曰：「固知崔樞辦之。

translations.literal: Later he told Jun: "I knew Cui Shu would handle it.
translations.idiomatic: Later he told Jun: "I knew Cui Shu would manage it.

sentences.zh: 縣殺賊子，為怨已大，人今自為戰矣。」

translations.literal: The county killed the bandits' sons and the grievance was already great — the people now fought for themselves."
translations.idiomatic: The county had killed the bandits' sons, deepening the feud — the people now fought on their own."

sentences.zh: 圓朗攻虞城，不能拔。

translations.literal: Yuanlang attacked Yucheng but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlang besieged Yucheng but could not capture it.

sentences.zh: 賊平，遷徐州總管，仍為大使。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified he was transferred as Commander of Xuzhou and continued as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were subdued he became Commander of Xuzhou and remained commissioner.

sentences.zh: 輔公祏反，詔以兵自揚子津濟江討之。

translations.literal: When Fu Gongshi rebelled an edict ordered him to cross the Yangzi from Yangzi Ford with troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Gongshi rebelled he was ordered to cross the Yangzi at Yangzi Ford to attack.

sentences.zh: 公祏平，拜邗州都督，遷陜州。

translations.literal: When Gongshi was pacified he was made Governor of Han and transferred to Shaan.
translations.idiomatic: After Gongshi was subdued he was Governor of Han, then transferred to Shaan.

sentences.zh: 瑰弟璨，為隱太子典膳監。

translations.literal: Gui's younger brother Can was Provision Director of the Hidden Crown Prince's household.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's brother Can was Provision Director for the Hidden Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 太子廢，璨得罪，瑰亦左授通州都督。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was deposed Can was punished and Gui was also demoted to Governor of Tong.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince fell Can was punished and Gui was demoted to Governor of Tong.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Zhenguan.

sentences.zh: 瑰歷職有功，然補吏多為親故人私，至負勢賕請，瑰知，不甚禁遏，世以此譏之。

translations.literal: Gui had merit in his offices, yet many subordinates he appointed were private kin and friends; he even accepted bribes by power — Gui knew but did not greatly restrain it, and the age reproached him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Gui served with merit, but many appointees were kin and friends; he tolerated bribery and favor-seeking, and the age criticized him.

sentences.zh: 瑰卒，時有司以在外對仗白奏，太宗怒曰：「昔杜如晦亡，朕不能事者數日。

translations.literal: When Gui died the relevant office reported facing the throne with staff in hand; Taizong angrily said: "When Du Ruhui died I could not attend to affairs for days.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui died the office reported in formal audience; Taizong said angrily: "When Du Ruhui died I could not work for days.

sentences.zh: 今瑰喪，所司不以狀言，豈朕意乎？

translations.literal: Now Gui is dead and the office does not report by memorial — is that my wish?
translations.idiomatic: Now Gui is dead and they do not report properly — is that what I want?

sentences.zh: 有如朕子弟不幸死，當此奏邪！」

translations.literal: If one of my sons or brothers should die unhappily, would you report it this way!
translations.idiomatic: If my own kin died, would you report it this way?

sentences.zh: 自是大臣喪，遂不對仗奏云。

translations.literal: From then on when great ministers died they no longer reported facing the throne with staff.
translations.idiomatic: After that great ministers' deaths were no longer announced in that formal manner.

sentences.zh: 丘和，河南洛陽人，後徙家郿。

translations.literal: Qiu He was a native of Luoyang in Henan and later moved his family to Mei.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu He came from Luoyang in Henan and later moved to Mei.

sentences.zh: 少重氣俠，閑弓馬，長乃折節自將。

translations.literal: In youth he valued chivalry, was skilled in bow and horse, and in maturity restrained himself.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was chivalrous and skilled in arms; in maturity he disciplined himself.

sentences.zh: 仕周開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He served Zhou as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Privileges Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou he was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Privileges Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 入隋為右武衛將軍，封平城郡公，歷資、梁、蒲三州刺史，以寬惠著名。

translations.literal: Entering Sui he was General of the Right Martial Guard, enfeoffed Duke of Pingcheng Commandery, and served as prefect of Zi, Liang, and Pu — famed for leniency and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui he was General of the Right Martial Guard, Duke of Pingcheng, and prefect of Zi, Liang, and Pu, famed for mild rule.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒反，使卒衣婦人衣，襲取蒲州，和挺身免，坐廢為民。

translations.literal: When Prince Han Liang rebelled he sent men in women's dress to seize Pu Prefecture; He escaped alone and was demoted to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Han rebelled, soldiers in women's dress seized Pu; He escaped and was reduced to commoner.

sentences.zh: 宇文述有寵，和傾心附納。

translations.literal: Yuwen Shu had favor; He devoted himself to attach to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shu was favored and He attached himself to him.

sentences.zh: 俄以發武陵公元胄罪，復拜代州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long, for exposing the crime of Prince of Wuling Yuan Chou, he was again made prefect of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, for exposing Prince Wuling Yuan Chou's crime, he was again prefect of Dai.

sentences.zh: 煬帝北巡，和饋獻精腆，至朔州，而刺史楊廓無所進，帝不悅。

translations.literal: When the emperor toured the north He presented refined provisions; reaching Shuozhou, Prefect Yang Kuo made no presentation and the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: On the northern tour He gave fine provisions; at Shuozhou Yang Kuo gave nothing and the emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 述盛稱和美，帝用為博陵太守，詔廓就視和為式。

translations.literal: Shu greatly praised He's excellence and the emperor used him as prefect of Boling, ordering Kuo to observe He's methods.
translations.idiomatic: Shu praised He and the emperor made him prefect of Boling, telling Kuo to learn from him.

sentences.zh: 後帝過博陵，和上食加豐，愈喜。

translations.literal: Later when the emperor passed Boling, He presented a richer feast and the emperor was still more pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor passed Boling again, He's feast was richer and the emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 由是所過競為珍侈獻，自和發也。

translations.literal: Thereupon every place he passed vied in presenting rare luxuries — it began with He.
translations.idiomatic: From then on every stop vied in luxury gifts — it began with He.

sentences.zh: 然和善撫吏士，得其心。

translations.literal: Yet He was good at comforting officials and soldiers and won their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet He won officials and soldiers by kindness.

sentences.zh: 遷天水郡守，入為左禦衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to command Tian Shui Commandery and entered the capital as General of the Left Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He became commandant of Tian Shui and entered as General of the Left Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 大業末，海南苦吏侵，數怨畔。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye Hainan suffered harsh officials and rebelled repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Daye Hainan suffered cruel officials and rebelled often.

sentences.zh: 帝以和所蒞稱淳良，而黃門侍郎裴矩亦薦之，遂拜交址太過，撫接盡情，荒憬安之。

translations.literal: The emperor because He's governance was called pure and Vice Director Pei Ju also recommended him, made him Grand Administrator of Jiaozhi; he comforted all with full heart and the wild frontiers were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, hearing He's rule was pure, and with Pei Ju's recommendation, made him Grand Administrator of Jiaozhi; he governed wholeheartedly and the frontier was calmed.

sentences.zh: 煬帝崩，而和未知。

translations.literal: When Yang died He did not yet know.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang died He had not yet heard.

sentences.zh: 於是鴻臚卿寧長真舉郁林附蕭銑，馮盎舉珠崖、番禺附林士弘，各遣使招和，不從。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chamberlain Ning Changzhen raised Yulin for Xiao Xian, Feng Ang raised Zhuya and Panyu for Lin Shihong — each sent envoys to win He and he would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Ning Changzhen joined Xiao Xian, Feng Ang joined Lin Shihong — each sent envoys; He refused.

sentences.zh: 林邑西諸國，數遺和明珠、文犀、金寶，故和富埒王者。

translations.literal: The western states of Linyi repeatedly sent He pearls, rhinoceros horn, gold, and treasures, so He was as rich as a king.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi and western states sent pearls, rhinoceros horn, and gold, and He grew as rich as a king.

sentences.zh: 銑聞，利之，命長真以南粵蠻、俚攻交址，和遣長史高士廉率兵擊走之，郡為樹石勒其功。

translations.literal: Xian heard and coveted this; he ordered Changzhen to attack Jiaozhi with southern Yue barbarians and Li; He sent Chief Clerk Gao Shilian with troops to repel them and the commandery set up a stone to record the merit.
translations.idiomatic: Xian coveted his wealth and sent Changzhen to attack with southern tribes; He sent Gao Shilian to repel them and erected a memorial stone.

sentences.zh: 會隋驍果自江都來，乃審隋亡，和即陳款歸國，而嶺嶠閉岨，乃權附銑。

translations.literal: When Sui crack troops came from Jiangdu he then learned Sui had fallen; He at once offered submission to the Tang, but the mountain passes were closed and he therefore temporarily attached to Xian.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui veterans came from Jiangdu he learned the dynasty had fallen; he submitted to Tang, but passes were closed and he temporarily joined Xian.

sentences.zh: 銑平，遂得歸。

translations.literal: When Xian was pacified he was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian fell he returned.

sentences.zh: 詔李道裕即授和交州大總管，爵譚國公。

translations.literal: An edict had Li Daoyu immediately appoint He Grand Commander of Jiaozhou and enfeoff him Duke of Tan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Commander of Jiaozhou and Duke of Tan.

sentences.zh: 和遣士廉奉表請入朝，詔其子師利迎之。

translations.literal: He sent Shilian to present a memorial requesting audience; an edict had his son Shili welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Shilian with a memorial to request audience; his son Shili was sent to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 及謁見，高祖為興，引入臥內，語平生，歡甚，奏九部樂饗之，除左武候大將軍。

translations.literal: On audience Gaozu rose, brought him into the sleeping quarters, spoke of old days with great joy, had the nine suites performed to feast him, and made him General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu rose to meet him, took him to his private chambers, reminisced joyfully, feasted him with the nine suites, and made him General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 和時已老，以稷州其故鄉也，令為刺史以自養。

translations.literal: He was already old; as Ji Prefecture was his old home he was made prefect to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was old; as Ji was his homeland he was made prefect to live out his days.

sentences.zh: 尋除特進。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十一年卒，年八十六，贈荊州總管，謚曰襄，陪葬獻陵。

translations.literal: He died in the eleventh year of Zhenguan at eighty-six, was posthumously made Governor of Jing with posthumous title Xiang, and buried beside Xianling.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhenguan year eleven at eighty-six, posthumously Governor of Jing with title Xiang, buried beside Xianling.

sentences.zh: 有子十五人，多至大官，而行恭為知名。

translations.literal: He had fifteen sons, many reaching high office, but Xinggong was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He had fifteen sons, many in high office; Xinggong was best known.

sentences.zh: 子行恭

translations.literal: The son Xinggong
translations.idiomatic: His son Xinggong

sentences.zh: 行恭有勇，善騎射。

translations.literal: Xinggong was brave and skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggong was brave and skilled in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 大業末，與兄師利聚兵萬人保郿城，人多依之，群盜不敢窺境。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he with his elder brother Shili gathered ten thousand men to hold Mei; many relied on them and bandits did not dare encroach.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Daye he and Shili raised ten thousand men to hold Mei; people flocked to them and bandits did not dare approach.

sentences.zh: 後原州奴賊圍扶風，太守竇璡堅守。

translations.literal: Later Yuan Prefecture slave rebels besieged Fufeng and Prefect Dou Jin held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Later slave rebels from Yuan besieged Fufeng while Prefect Dou Jin held out.

sentences.zh: 賊食盡無所掠，眾稍散歸行恭。

translations.literal: The rebels' food was exhausted with nothing to plunder and the masses gradually dispersed back to Xinggong.
translations.idiomatic: When their food ran out the rebels dispersed toward Xinggong.

sentences.zh: 行恭遣其酋說賊共迎高祖，乃自率五百人負糧持牛酒詣賊營。

translations.literal: Xinggong sent their chiefs to urge the rebels jointly to welcome Gaozu; he himself led five hundred men carrying grain, cattle, and wine to the rebel camp.
translations.idiomatic: He sent chiefs to urge them to welcome Gaozu, then led five hundred men with grain, cattle, and wine to the camp.

sentences.zh: 奴帥長揖，行恭手斬之，謂眾曰：「若皆豪桀也，何為事奴乎？

translations.literal: The slave chief gave a long bow; Xinggong cut him down by hand and told the crowd: "If you are all heroes, why serve slaves?
translations.idiomatic: The slave leader bowed; Xinggong struck him down and said: "If you are heroes, why serve as slaves?

sentences.zh: 使天下號曰奴賊。」

translations.literal: Let the realm call you slave rebels no more.
translations.idiomatic: Let the realm no longer call you slave rebels.

sentences.zh: 眾皆伏，曰：「願改事公。」

translations.literal: The crowd all submitted and said: "We wish to serve you instead."
translations.idiomatic: All submitted: "We wish to serve you."

sentences.zh: 行恭乃率其眾，與師利迎謁秦王於渭北，拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Xinggong then led his masses with Shili to welcome the Prince of Qin on the north bank of the Wei and was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He led them with Shili to welcome the Prince of Qin north of the Wei and was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 累從戰伐，功多，遷左一府驃騎，錫勞甚厚。

translations.literal: He followed repeatedly in campaigns with many achievements, was transferred to Swift Cavalry of the Left First Office, and received rich rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He fought on many campaigns, rose to Swift Cavalry of the Left First Office, and was richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 隱太子誅，以功擢左衛將軍。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Crown Prince was executed he was raised for merit to General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After the crown prince's fall he was raised to General of the Left Guard for merit.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，坐與兄爭葬所生母，廢為民。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan, for quarreling with his brother over burying their birth mother, he was demoted to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan he quarreled with his brother over their mother's burial and was reduced to commoner.

sentences.zh: 從侯君集平高昌，封天水郡公，進右武候將軍。

translations.literal: Following Hou Junji in pacifying Gaochang he was enfeoffed Duke of Tian Shui Commandery and advanced to General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Hou Junji against Gaochang, was enfeoffed Duke of Tian Shui, and made General of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 高宗立，遷大將軍、冀陜二州刺史，致仕。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne he was transferred as Grand General and prefect of Ji and Shaan, then retired.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong he was Grand General and prefect of Ji and Shaan, then retired.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十，贈荊州刺史，謚曰襄，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: He died at eighty, was posthumously made Governor of Jing with posthumous title Xiang, and buried beside Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty, posthumously Governor of Jing with title Xiang, buried beside Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 行恭所守嚴烈，僚吏畏之。

translations.literal: Xinggong's governance was stern and fierce and subordinates feared him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was stern and subordinates feared him.

sentences.zh: 數坐事免，太宗思其功，不逾時輒復官。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly dismissed for offenses yet Taizong remembered his merit and before long restored him.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed repeatedly, he was soon restored each time for his old service.

sentences.zh: 初，從討王世充，戰邙山。

translations.literal: At first, following the campaign against Wang Shichong, they fought at Mount Mang.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, campaigning against Wang Shichong, they fought at Mount Mang.

sentences.zh: 太宗欲嘗賊虛實，與數十騎沖出陣後，多所殺傷，而限長堤，與諸騎相失，唯行恭從。

translations.literal: Taizong wished to test the enemy's strength and with several dozen horsemen charged behind the enemy lines, killing many; but a long embankment separated him from the other riders — only Xinggong followed.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong probed the enemy with a few dozen riders, charging behind their lines; a long dike cut him off from the others — only Xinggong followed.

sentences.zh: 賊騎追及，流矢著太宗馬，行恭回射之，發無虛鏃，賊不敢前。

translations.literal: Enemy cavalry caught up; a stray arrow struck Taizong's horse; Xinggong turned and shot — none missed — and the enemy did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy horsemen caught up; an arrow hit Taizong's horse; Xinggong shot back without missing and they held back.

sentences.zh: 遂下拔箭，以己馬進太宗，步執長刀，大呼導之，斬數人，突陣而還。

translations.literal: He then dismounted, pulled the arrow, gave Taizong his own horse, took a long blade on foot, shouted to guide him, cut down several men, and burst back through the lines.
translations.idiomatic: He pulled the arrow, gave Taizong his horse, took a long blade on foot, cut a path through the enemy, and broke back to the lines.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，詔斫石為人馬，象拔箭狀，立昭陵闕前，以旌武功云。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan an edict carved stone men and horses showing the arrow-pulling scene before Zhaoling's gate to commemorate martial achievement.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan stone figures of man and horse showing the arrow scene were set before Zhaoling to honor his valor.

sentences.zh: 子神勣，見《酷吏傳》。

translations.literal: His son Shenji is treated in the Biography of Cruel Officials.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shenji appears in the Biography of Cruel Officials.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：帝王之將興，其威靈氣焰有以動物悟人者，故士有一概，皆填然躍而附之，若榱椽梁柱以成大室，又負偃植，各安所施而無遺材，諸將之謂邪。

translations.literal: The comment says: When an emperor is about to rise, his awesomeness and numinous force move things and awaken men; therefore scholars with one resolve all surge to attach themselves, like rafters and beams completing a great hall — each placed where it fits without wasted timber. Such were these generals.
translations.idiomatic: The comment says: When a dynasty rises, its aura moves men to rally like timbers fitting a hall — each general finding his place. Such were these men.

sentences.zh: 然皆能禮法自完，賢矣哉！

translations.literal: Yet all could preserve themselves through ritual and law — how worthy!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet all kept themselves within ritual and law — admirable indeed!"
